components.note: 亻 (person) — 优 originally described an outstanding performer or actor
尤 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 优's reading yōu
隹 (short-tailed bird) — 雅 originally named a type of crow, later borrowed for the unrelated meaning 'elegant, refined.'
牙 (yá) gives a sound close to yǎ, sharing the same syllable body and differing only in tone.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'
毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).
土 (earth) — 埃 names fine dust or dirt.
矣 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to āi, having drifted apart over time.
巾 (cloth) — 幕 names a large piece of cloth, a curtain or screen.
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to mù, sharing the same rhyme.
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
犭 (dog) — an old link behind 独's meaning 'alone, single, solitary'
虫 (chóng) gives a loose sound connection to 独's reading dú
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
矢 (arrow) — 医 originally related to treating arrow wounds, the root of its meaning 'to cure, doctor'
匸 gives a loose sound connection to 医's reading yī
页 (head) — 额 names the forehead, part of the head.
客 (kè) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading é has diverged considerably.

口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.
A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'
扌 (hand) — 扰 describes stirring something up by hand, 'to disturb.'
尤 (yóu) is only distantly related in sound to rǎo — the connection has drifted apart over time.
冫 (ice) — melting ice shrinks away, an image linked to 减's meaning 'to decrease.'
咸 (xián) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading jiǎn has diverged.
少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'

meanings: rent for a room or house

components.note: 户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match
禾 (grain) — 租 originally described tribute paid in grain.
且 here marks the payment as regular and ongoing — combined with the grain 禾, it gave 租 its meaning 'rent, tax.'
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone
阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 防 is also pronounced fáng, a close match
宀 (walls/roof) — the boundary of a home to be protected
寸 (a hand) — keeping watch, holding the space within the walls
欠 (to lack) shows 欺 relates to taking advantage of a lack or weakness in someone.
其 (qí) gives a sound close to qī, differing mainly in tone.
人 — a person, shown bending over
贝 (money/shell) — a heavy load of money the person is carrying on their back
扌 (hand) — 挽 describes pulling or drawing something back with the hand.
免 (miǎn) gives a sound distantly related to 挽's reading wǎn, having drifted apart over time.
攵 (a hand taking action) — 救 describes the act of rescuing someone.
求 (qiú) gives a sound close to jiù, sharing a similar rhyme.
攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.

扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.

广 (shelter) pictures a roofed building.
车 (cart) sits inside, together giving 库 its meaning 'storehouse, warehouse.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

meanings: to give birth to a child

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'
攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
矢 (arrow) — 医 originally related to treating arrow wounds, the root of its meaning 'to cure, doctor'
匸 gives a loose sound connection to 医's reading yī

刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'
⺼ (flesh, body) — 脱 relates to taking something off the body.
兑 (duì) gives a sound close to tuō, sharing a related initial.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'
酉 (wine, alcohol) — 酗 relates to being drunk, as in 酗酒 (xùjiǔ), to drink excessively.
凶 (vicious, ominous) — captures the aggressive or dangerous behavior that can come with drunkenness, as in 酗酒 leading to violence.
酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
贝 (money) shows 贷 relates to a financial transaction.
代 (dài) gives the exact sound of 贷.
欠 (to owe/lack) — 款 relates to funds, especially money owed or paid

刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè
羊 (sheep) — 羞 pairs a sheep with the idea of something unsightly.
丑 (ugly, shameful) contributes to the character's form, giving 羞 its meaning 'ashamed, shy.'
口 (mouth) — 哈 is the sound made by the mouth while laughing
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 哈's reading hā, from an older, closer pronunciation link
罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
彐 (a hand reaching out) — 寻 relates to searching, reaching for something.
寸 (cùn) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading xún has diverged.
巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

十 (shí) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zhì.

矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating

旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to dǎn, differing only in tone.

大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.

meanings: (to work or fight) as if one's life depends on it

components.note: Hand — putting pieces together by hand.
Gives the sound bìng, related to pīn but drifted apart over time.
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'
木 (wood) — 枕 originally named a wooden headrest.
冘 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to zhěn, having drifted apart over time.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
禾 (a grain plant) — a sweet-smelling crop
日 — here standing in for sweetness (originally 甘), giving the sense of a pleasant smell
水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.

卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

波 (bō) gives a sound close to pó, sharing the same rhyme.

金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

辶 (to walk/move) — 速 relates to the speed of movement
束 (shù) gives a loose sound connection to 速's reading sù
